blocks.text: Why document processing is a major paralegal headache

You likely spend a significant part of your day dealing with scanned PDFs, discovery files, and pleadings. When these files are just images, you cannot search for specific Bates numbers or names. This forces you to read through pages manually. This process is slow and prone to human error. It also takes you away from higher-level work that requires your legal expertise.
The true cost of manual document handling

Manual document processing is not just a nuisance. It has real financial and emotional costs for your firm. When you spend hours retyping text from a scan, you are not performing billable work. Small firms often lose thousands of dollars in monthly revenue due to these inefficiencies. Worse, the pressure to maintain perfect accuracy while managing high volumes of files creates chronic stress. This contributes to the high rate of burnout reported by legal professionals.

blocks.text: Fixes you can use right now

You do not need expensive enterprise software to start improving your workflow. Start by standardizing how you name and store files. Use consistent naming conventions that include the date and case number. Move files from local folders to a centralized cloud location that your team shares. This creates a single source of truth for every case.
Always check your firm's policy on handling client data before uploading documents to any cloud service or third-party tool. Security is paramount.
blocks.title: Protecting client data

blocks.text: How OCR for legal documents changes the game

OCR, or Optical Character Recognition, is the technology that makes images readable. By using OCR on your Mac, you can turn a scanned PDF into a text-searchable document. Once you do this, you can press ⌘ + F in any PDF viewer to find specific terms instantly. This eliminates the need to scan pages with your eyes.

faq.question: Is OCR accurate enough for legal documents?
faq.answer: Modern OCR tools are highly accurate, but they can still make mistakes with handwritten notes or poor quality scans. Always review the output for critical documents.

faq.question: How do I ensure my OCR process is secure?
faq.answer: Use local, Mac-native apps for OCR whenever possible to keep your data on your machine. If you use cloud-based tools, ensure they comply with your firm's security and privacy standards.

faq.question: Does Lazur perform the OCR for me?
faq.answer: No, Lazur does not perform OCR. Lazur is a voice assistant that helps you navigate your apps, find tools, and answer questions about how to use them effectively.
